title: Automated decommission pipeline for PII with verifiable deletion receipts
creator: Lina Chen
description: Design and deliver an automated decommission pipeline that executes tenant-scoped permanent deletion for PII and generates cryptographically verifiable deletion receipts customers can use as proof-of-erasure. The pipeline must operate across multi-region stores (hot KV, object storage, backups) and produce an auditable deliverable for legal/compliance requests without exposing internal logs or customer data.
acceptance_criteria: API: Customers can create a deletion request via /v1/deletion-requests and receive a deletion_id immediately.
Execution: Backend workers process deletion requests, delete primary and cached copies, and schedule secondary store cleanup (snapshots/backups) according to configured retention windows.

Receipt: Upon completion, system emits a signed deletion receipt containing deletion_id, scope (tenant/region), object_count, aggregate_hash, timestamp, and signature. The receipt must be verifiable against a published public key.
Observability: Deletion lifecycle is visible in Console with per-request timelines, status (Queued, Deleting, Completed, Failed), and links to the signed receipt and raw audit bundle.
Compliance export: Admins can export an evidence bundle (JSONL) with per-store operation events and immutable attestations for at least 1 year by default.
SLO: 95% of standard tenant-scoped deletion requests for datasets < 2M rows complete within 24 hours; larger datasets should have an estimated completion time provided.
Safety: Legal-hold and designated retention labels prevent deletion; attempts to delete held data return a clear reason and audit entry.
Security: Signing keys are protected by KMS/HSM and rotation events are captured in the audit trail.
Tests: End-to-end integration tests validate deletion across hot store, object store, and a snapshot restore attempt confirming objects are irrecoverable after confirmed deletion completion.
implementation_notes: Architectural pattern: declarative deletion job -> orchestrator -> per-store executors (KV executor, S3 executor, backup executor)
Receipt format: JSON with fields (deletion_id, tenant_id, scope, object_count, aggregate_sha256, deleted_store_map, completed_at_iso, signer_key_id, signature_base64)
Signature: use asymmetric signing via AWS KMS or customer-managed HSM; publish corresponding public keys for verification endpoints.

Immutable evidence: append-only ledger stored in a Write-Ahead-Log S3 prefix with S3 Object Lock (governance mode) for audit retention; ledger entries reference deletion receipts and per-store operation checksums.
Idempotency: deletion requests must be idempotent and safe to retry; maintain job state machine with tombstones to prevent double-signing receipts.
Legal hold integration: consult retention service to short-circuit deletes and emit related audit events; surface hold metadata to users in the API response.
Backups: implement staggered purge plan for historical backups with owner-configurable windows; include proof of scheduling and final deletion events in evidence bundle.
On-prem connectors: define a connector contract for customers running Redwood Private to export local deletion events and exchange signed receipts via a secure webhook or signed bundle download.

risks: Cross-store consistency: ensuring all copies (caches, replicas, backups) are irrecoverable is technically challenging and may require longer retention windows for backups.
Performance: large-scale deletions can spike I/O and impact tenant throughput if not throttled; need conservative defaults and quotas.
Legal: regulatory requirements differ by jurisdiction; we must avoid auto-deleting when a lawful hold exists or when exports are required.
Verification: customers will rely on receipts; signature compromise would be high-impact — requires strict KMS/HSM controls and monitoring.
qa_plan: Unit tests for per-store executor idempotency and state transitions.
Integration tests that simulate a full deletion request across hot store, object storage, and simulated backup store; validate receipt signature and inability to restore deleted objects.
Chaos test: kill executor pods mid-delete to validate retry logic and single final receipt semantics.
Compliance test: sample evidence bundle reviewed by legal to ensure export contains required metadata and is human-auditable.
Load test: issue 1k concurrent small deletion requests and measure SLO compliance and system resource usage.
rollback_plan: If a regression is detected in deletion correctness or signing integrity, disable automated receipts (feature flag) and revert to manual audited deletion workflows. Notify affected customers per incident policy and preserve current ledger for forensic analysis.
